reason: The schedule's premise is wrong. It says CI kernels queue 2-3.3 h on Kaggle while secFT and DIV kernels start at once. The latest CI dummy disproves that as a rule. `kaggle kernels list --mine` gives lastRunTime = run start: exp75 was pushed 13:18Z and shows 16:41:50Z, matching R19-A1 (4). exp79a has the same datasets (incl. yuki0731/biohub-coord-inject), the same T4 shape and the same docker as exp75/exp76a. It was still 404 at 20:28Z and started at 20:32:27Z, so it waited at most ~4 min. It started 26 s after exp79d ended (20:10:16Z + ~1,305 s), while exp77 (T4x2, 19:04-21:24Z) held the other lane. exp81 and exp80a then both started at 21:26Z, right after exp77 ended. So the account runs 2 GPU lanes at once, and a queue comes from lane contention or a random Kaggle-side delay. It is not a property of CI. The afternoon waits (exp75 ~3.3 h, exp76a ~2 h) were real. But non-CI kernels also ran in that window (exp72 13:27Z, exp76d 16:07Z), and the next CI kernel did not repeat them. That breaks the plan in two ways. (1) The speculative early push is justified only for CI, but a random queue would hit the lazily scheduled SEC-on-holder dummies too: exp82b ~07:50Z and exp82a ~08:40Z sit on the W2a 08:45-10:00Z critical path with no margin. (2) The quota triage (priority list, 'above 26 h used: only exp83a and FULL*') solves a problem we do not have. By my count the usage is 07:55 at 26 Sep 21:5xZ plus ~11.4 h of kernels since then (exp71 and exp77 are the two big ones), about 19.5-21 h used and ~9-10.5 h left. That is ~6 h left even if T4x2 bills double. The weekly reset is Sat 3 Oct, after the deadline, so any quota left unused is worthless, and the worst case of ~3 h fits either way. Feasibility is fine otherwise. Dummies are not submits; the builds reproduce byte-identically (scan notes); hidden reruns do not use quota or lanes (CONTEXT l.1972). The FULL*/exp84a clauses match table v3 (8). Value is ~0 LB; the only benefit is slot hygiene. In short, the direction (push the exp83a dummy tonight) survives, but the lazy/speculative split and the quota ranking rest on a refuted asymmetry.
